sections.title: Overview: Laws for Covenant Community Life

blocks.text: Deuteronomy 24 comprises case laws addressing household relations, creditor obligations, and community practices. These regulations form part of the covenant instruction in Deuteronomy 5-26, where Moses expounds the covenant obligations binding the generation poised to enter the promised land.

Deuteronomy's covenant framework joins exclusive allegiance to YHWH with justice and deliberate care for vulnerable community members. The Torah is presented as instruction shaping household economics, community relations, and worship. Even specific case laws participate in this covenantal vision of shared communal life.

Deuteronomy's narrated setting is the plains of Moab east of the Jordan in the fortieth year of wilderness wandering. Moses addresses the successor generation to those who received the covenant at Horeb, speaking as though the covenant's past and present obligations belong to them as they prepare to cross into the land.
